question: What sort of papers were considered important by Rao?

options.text: Title-deeds, diaries, papers and a will

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** passage mentions** that Rao kept his important papers stacked in an almirah, which he kept locked.
 
• These important papers are **described as **containing virtually all the clues to his life.
 
• It further states that Rao occasionally accessed these papers, which were stored in the almirah.
 
• The passage** specifically mentions title-deeds, diaries, papers, and a will **as the contents of the other cupboard that Rao would open.
 
• Therefore, it can be inferred that these documents, including title-deeds, diaries, papers, and a will, were considered important by Rao.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is-* 'Title-deeds, diaries, papers and a will'. *
